label: prop:gram-degeneracy-blocks-connes
title: A Lipschitz seminorm with nonzero kernel has no finite Connes sup
html:
Let L be a Lipschitz seminorm on an algebra of observables, let \varphi and \psi be states, and let

  d(\varphi,\psi) \;=\; \sup\,\bigl\{\, |\varphi(a) - \psi(a)| \;:\; L(a) \le 1 \,\bigr\}

be the associated Connes distance. If some k satisfies L(k) = 0 while \varphi(k) \ne \psi(k), then the supremum is unbounded: for every proposed bound M there is an admissible b with |\varphi(b) - \psi(b)| > M.

The argument in one line

Homogeneity and subadditivity give L(a + tk) \le L(a) + |t|\,L(k) = L(a), so the whole line a + tk stays inside the unit ball of the seminorm, while the objective

  \varphi(a+tk) - \psi(a+tk)
  \;=\; \bigl(\varphi(a)-\psi(a)\bigr) \;+\; t\,\bigl(\varphi(k)-\psi(k)\bigr)

grows linearly in t. Choosing t large enough overshoots any bound. The distance is +\infty as posed, not a hard computation.

Stating the conclusion as "no upper bound exists" rather than "d = \infty" keeps the statement inside an ordered field, with no top element adjoined.

Why the framework runs into it

The natural candidate for a derived metric on the state space is the Gram form of the Markov trace: build a Lipschitz seminorm from it, take the Connes supremum, and read off a distance. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) that route is blocked before it starts. The star form is positive semidefinite with a one-dimensional kernel --- the block killed by the row cap --- and a kernel of the form is a kernel of the seminorm. Any state pair separating that direction supplies the k above.

The obstruction is a fact about the method, and it names its own repair: quotient by the radical, or choose a different seminorm.

Prior art and structural synthesis

The metric formula combines the primal--dual optimal transport duality of Leonid V. Kantorovich [kantorovich1942] and Gennady Sh. Rubinstein [rubinstein1957] with the noncommutative spectral distance of Alain Connes [connes1989, connes1994], recast in order-unit generality by Marc A. Rieffel [rieffel1999, rieffel2004] and linked to Wasserstein transport by Francesco D'Andrea and Pierre Martinetti [dandrea-martinetti2010]. On any order-unit algebra, Rieffel's Lip-norm theorem establishes that d(\varphi,\psi) defines a finite state-space metric if and only if \ker L reduces to scalar multiples of the identity [rieffel1999, latremoliere2016]; Bruno Iochum, Thomas Krajewski, and Pierre Martinetti [iochum-krajewski-martinetti2001] track the resulting infinite-distance walls on finite-dimensional algebras whenever the representation kernel is non-trivial, together with the finite shortest-path distance recovered on the faithful quotient. Passing modulo the null ideal \mathcal{N}_\tau implements the operational indiscernibility quotient of Israel M. Gelfand, Mark A. Naimark, and Irving E. Segal [gelfand-naimark1943, segal1947] (extended to physical equivalence by Rudolf Haag and Daniel Kastler [haag-kastler1964]) and mirrors quotienting by the presymplectic gauge null radical in the formalism of Marc Henneaux and Claudio Teitelboim [henneaux-teitelboim1992].

Two structural features distinguish how this quotient operates here from its standard appearances in topological field theory and noncommutative geometry. First, universal skein and categorical semisimplification quotients --- developed by Christian Blanchet, Nathan Habegger, Gregor Masbaum, and Pierre Vogel [bhmv1995] and by John W. Barrett and Bruce W. Westbury [barrett1993] --- specialise q to a root of unity e^{i\pi/r} to annihilate tilting modules of zero quantum dimension; here q > 1 lies on the real hyperbolic ray where U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) is semisimple, and the Markov trace radical arises from Michio Jimbo's two-row \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Schur--Weyl rank cap [jimbo1986], which sets the Young-diagram trace weights of Vaughan F. R. Jones [jones1987], Hans Wenzl [wenzl1988], Rosa C. Orellana [orellana1998], and Meinolf Geck and Sofia Lambropoulou [geck-lambropoulou-2004] to zero on every partition with \ell(\lambda) \ge 3, leaving the planar algebra of Harold Neville Vazeille Temperley and Elliott H. Lieb [temperley-lieb1971]. Second, spectral Standard Model geometries [chamseddine-connes-1997] posit a semisimple finite algebra \mathbb{C} \oplus \mathbb{H} \oplus M_3(\mathbb{C}) with a faithful trace by stipulation; here the derivation starts on H_n(q) at real q_0 > 1, proves that the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) forces \det G = 0 for n \ge 3, and uses Rieffel's kernel criterion so that state-space metric finiteness dynamically forces the projection H_n(q) \twoheadrightarrow TL_n(q).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 for z = q^3/(q^2+1) the star-form spectrum is 0,\, 0.752702^{\times 3},\, 4.230339: exactly one null direction, and it is the braid-symmetric one.
